shorts.title: The Secret Nuclear Base Under Greenland's Ice 🧊 Case #15
shorts.description:
A town under Greenland's ice ran on a nuclear reactor. Camp Century, dug into the Greenland ice sheet in 1959 and powered by a portable nuclear reactor, was the public face of Project Iceworm: a secret US Army plan for 4,000 km of ice tunnels holding up to 600 nuclear missiles. The moving ice made it unworkable, and the camp was abandoned in the 1960s. Its waste is still under the ice.

shorts.title: Mike the Headless Chicken Was REAL 🐓 Case #16 Meatball Investigates
shorts.description:
A farmer swung an axe, and the rooster walked away. On 10 September 1945 in Fruita, Colorado, farmer Lloyd Olsen's axe missed the jugular and left one ear and most of the brain stem, so Mike the rooster lived another 18 months. Olsen fed him with an eyedropper and toured him at sideshows. Fruita still holds Mike the Headless Chicken Day every May.

#shorts #meatballinvestigates #weirdhistory #mystery #meatballmyths

shorts.title: Britain Planned an Aircraft Carrier Made of ICE 🧊 Case #17
shorts.description:
Britain designed an aircraft carrier out of ice, and Churchill loved it. Project Habakkuk: in WWII Geoffrey Pyke proposed an unsinkable aircraft carrier made of pykrete, frozen water mixed with wood pulp, which is tougher and slower-melting than plain ice. Churchill and Mountbatten backed it, and a 1,000-ton prototype was built on Patricia Lake in Canada in 1944 before the project was shelved.

shorts.title: Britain Planned an Aircraft Carrier Made of ICE 🧊 Case #17
shorts.description:
An officer pulled out his pistol in a meeting full of generals, and shot a block of ice. Project Habakkuk: a WWII British plan for an aircraft carrier made of pykrete (ice mixed with wood pulp). Churchill and Mountbatten backed it; a 1,000-ton prototype was built on Patricia Lake, Alberta, in 1944; the full ship would have displaced 2.2 million tons. At the 1943 Quebec Conference a bullet fired at a pykrete block reportedly ricocheted past Admiral Ernest King.

shorts.title: The 'Well to Hell': Did Scientists Hear Screams? 🔥 Case #18
shorts.description:
Soviet scientists drilled seven miles down, and a story said they heard screams. The Kola Superdeep Borehole in Russia reached 12,262 metres (about 7.6 miles) in 1989, the deepest hole ever drilled. Drilling stopped when rock temperatures hit about 180 °C, and the hole is now welded shut under a rusty metal cap. The 'screams from hell' story has no scientific record behind it.

#shorts #meatballinvestigates #weirdhistory #mystery #meatballmyths

shorts.title: MKUltra: The CIA Mind-Control Program Was REAL 🔍 Case #19
shorts.description:
The CIA ordered its files destroyed. Twenty thousand pages survived. MKUltra was a CIA program (1953 to the early 1970s) that tested drugs and other methods on people, some of them unwitting. Director Richard Helms ordered its files destroyed in 1973, but about 20,000 documents survived because they were misfiled with financial records, and a 1977 FOIA request found them.

shorts.title: The 1962 Laughter Epidemic Was REAL 😂 Case #20 Meatball Investigates
shorts.description:
Three schoolgirls started laughing, and couldn't stop. The Tanganyika laughter epidemic began on 30 January 1962 at a girls' boarding school in Kashasha, near Lake Victoria in what is now Tanzania. It started with three girls, spread to about 1,000 people and closed 14 schools before dying out about 18 months later. Researchers class it as mass psychogenic illness (mass hysteria), not an infection.

shorts.title: The Great Emu War of 1932 Was REAL 🪖 Case #21 Meatball Investigates
shorts.description:
Soldiers drove out with machine guns to fight an army of birds. In late 1932 the Australian Army sent soldiers with two Lewis machine guns to cull about 20,000 emus eating Western Australian wheat. The birds split into small groups, a gun jammed, and the operation was withdrawn. Defence Minister Sir George Pearce was later mocked in parliament as the 'Minister of the Emu War'.
